key_insight: Constrained, discrete plastic activation events in a rate-independent system can by themselves drive localized deformation and produce shear bands.
engineering_relevance: This provides a rigorous basis for modeling localized plasticity and shear-band initiation in materials where inelastic evolution occurs through intermittent, quantized events rather than smooth flow.
method: Formulate rate-independent evolution as incremental minimization of elastic energy plus one-homogeneous dissipation.
Impose admissible increment constraints to represent localized activation events in shear-transformation zones.
Analyze a lattice-based 2D shear-transformation-zone model and prove localization along a growing line segment in the continuum limit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a mathematical existence result for the continuous-time limit and a proof that the model localizes into shear bands in both infinite-domain and sufficiently large bounded-domain settings.
watch_item: The mechanism is proven for a simplified constrained model, so transferring it to more detailed constitutive laws or finite meshes may require careful validation.
paper_title: Formation of shear bands through discrete localized plastic increments
